主要内容: Noble Group, a troubled commodities trader, warned of a massive annual loss of $4.78 billion to $4.98 billion, citing challenging operating conditions. The company is racing to finalize a $3.4 billion debt-for-equity swap to ensure its survival. Noble announced a deal with creditors last month to halve its senior debt and give them 70 percent of the company, while existing equity holders would see their stake diluted to 10 percent. The company expects a total net loss of $1.72 billion to $1.92 billion for the quarter ending December 2017, stemming largely from non-cash losses from its mark-to-market derivatives portfolio. Noble's chairman, Paul Brough, said the company is looking forward to the final phase of its restructuring, aiming to create a new Noble as a focused and appropriately financed group set to capitalize on the high-growth Asian commodities sector. Noble also mentioned that the Ad Hoc Group, a group of senior creditors, held about 36 percent of the company's senior bonds and loans, with additional support from creditors holding about 15 percent of the senior debt instruments.
